name: Guardian genius crossword No 152
preamble: Solutions to 13 clues include sequences of letters of varying lengths not indicated in the wordplay. These sequences are all of a kind.

solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Turning head, see about top issue

indicators.note: one word goes about another, wrapping round it on both sides
the head of the built word is turned round, so its opening pair of letters swap places

blocks.note: taken as written
a cap is a top, as on a bottle

explanation.surface: An editor spinning round to check the main story in the next edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning head' turns only the head: the first two letters of the built word change places, not the whole word.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue is to flow out or emerge from somewhere, which is how gas or water will escape.

clue.text: Sort of acid (blah, blah, blah)

blocks.note: etc. stands for the rest of the tedious list, like blah blah blah
one of the capital cities the preamble hides, unclued: the capital of Vietnam

explanation.surface: Someone droning on and on about a particular acid.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble's thirteen unclued sequences are all capital cities; one of them is tucked inside this entry, with nothing in the clue for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethanoic acid is the chemist's name for acetic acid, the sharp component of vinegar.

clue.text: Day visiting Greek island? They'll likely be drawn

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside a place, so one word is put within the other

blocks.note: Cos (Kos) is an island in the Dodecanese
Mon is the abbreviation for Monday
an unclued capital city, as the preamble says: the capital of France

explanation.surface: A day-tripper's trip to a Greek island invites inevitable comparisons with home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawn' suggests pictures of the island; comparisons are drawn in the sense of made.
explanation.definitionFit: People commonly draw comparisons between two things, so comparisons are what is drawn.

clue.text: Way to waste time that is contemptible!

indicators.note: to waste something is to lose or throw it away, so that letter goes

blocks.note: a path is a way
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone sneering at a pastime as an idle waste of hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Pah is an exclamation of scorn, the noise someone makes on finding a thing beneath them.

clue.text: Good, Devon and Cornwall overturned action

definitions.note: the answer is plural; action here is industrial action in general

indicators.note: something overturned is upside down, so in an across clue it is read backwards

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
an unclued capital city, as the preamble says: the capital of Norway
these counties make up the South West of England

explanation.surface: A government in the West Country defeated over some decision.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon and Cornwall are the south-western tip of England, abbreviated SW.
explanation.definitionFit: Go-slows are a form of industrial action in which workers deliberately slow their output.

clue.text: Architectural feature's old, very old, look!

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
V is the abbreviation for very
O for old again, then lo, an old word for look

explanation.surface: A guide pointing out an ancient piece of a building with excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovolo is a convex moulding, roughly a quarter-circle in section, used in classical buildings.

clue.text: American's apparently neutral deity

indicators.note: what is apparent is plainly visible, here sitting in plain view inside the next word

blocks.note: the closing letters of the word, read upwards in this down entry

explanation.surface: An American god who seems to take no side.
explanation.walkthrough: No word signals the turnaround; in a down entry the letters simply read upwards from the end of the word. The role of 'American’s' is unclear and it is treated here as padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A lar was a Roman household god, one of the lares who guarded the family home.

clue.text: Greer's kind in pool not making either end?

indicators.note: failing to reach either end means the first and last letters are lost

blocks.note: what someone in a pool is doing

explanation.surface: A feminist swimmer in the pool who never reaches the end of a length.
explanation.walkthrough: Germaine Greer is the Australian feminist author of The Female Eunuch.
explanation.definitionFit: Wimmin is a feminist respelling of women, avoiding the word men, so it names the sex Greer championed.

clue.text: Calculating pair admitting love, opening whisky dispenser

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece is placed inside the other
a thing opened up has room made in its middle for something to enter

blocks.note: an optic is the measuring device on an upturned bottle in a bar
PR is the abbreviation for pair
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
an unclued capital city, as the preamble says: the capital of Tunisia

explanation.surface: A scheming couple in a bar letting love in while working the whisky optic.
explanation.walkthrough: An optic is a British pub fitting that pours a measured shot of spirit; it opens after its first two letters to hold the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A calculating person exploits openings for their own gain, which is exactly opportunistic behaviour.

clue.text: Women on stage overdoing hoax savage in act

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for women
to ham is to overact
bam is an old word for a hoax or trick

explanation.surface: A comic turn in which actresses overplay a practical joke with violence.
explanation.definitionFit: Wham-bam describes something abrupt and forceful, as in a hasty, rough act of sex.

clue.text: Circus in school

blocks.note: hip means fashionable, as does in
a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
an unclued capital city, as the preamble says: the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: Pupils staging a circus at their school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' looks like a building but is a group of whales, a pod.
explanation.definitionFit: A hippodrome is an arena for horse shows or a circus, from the Greek racecourse.

clue.text: Old ruler conspiring with night owl cries off

indicators.note: these noises are taken off, removed from the end of the phrase

blocks.note: in cahoots means conspiring together
owls hoot at night

explanation.surface: An ancient king plotting, with the owls' calls cancelled for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca was the emperor of the Andean empire conquered by Spain in the sixteenth century.

clue.text: Thick-skinned types take in hot drink

indicators.note: something taken in is held within the other word

blocks.note: cocoa is a hot drink
R stands for recipe, Latin take, on prescriptions
an unclued capital city, as the preamble says: the capital of East Timor

explanation.surface: Insensitive people who simply take a hot drink in their stride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thick-skinned' looks like insensitive people; it is literal, for armoured reptiles.
explanation.definitionFit: Crocodilia is the order of reptiles with thick scaly hides: crocodiles, alligators and gharials.

clue.text: $100 on head of sex god's a sizeable wedge

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
a hunk is a muscular, attractive man

explanation.surface: A hundred dollars staked on a heartthrob makes a decent wad of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, C on the head of HUNK sits above it.
explanation.definitionFit: A chunk is a thick, substantial piece of something, like a solid wedge of cheese.

clue.text: "Part of Campania" is sign over football club on day of pranks

blocks.note: taken as written
Leo is a sign of the zodiac
FC is the abbreviation for football club
April Fools' Day is APR 1, the 1 written as I

explanation.surface: A star sign hanging over a football club's April Fools' stunt in southern Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The date April 1 is written APR 1, with the digit read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples, which lies in the Italian region of Campania.

clue.text: Admitted to "retro" University, one's exhibiting cunning with wickedness

indicators.note: retro means looking back, so the words after it are read backwards

blocks.note: someone admitted is in
U is the abbreviation for university
I is the Roman numeral one
an unclued capital city, as the preamble says: the capital of Ecuador
sly means cunning

explanation.surface: A student accepted at an old-fashioned university who shows crafty, wicked behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: U and I turn round to give IU, and the unclued QUITO is slotted between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Iniquitously means acting in a grossly unjust or immoral manner, the adverb of iniquity.

clue.text: Withdraw organisation with HQ in New York, perhaps

blocks.clueFragment: organisation with HQ in New York
blocks.note: the United Nations has its headquarters in New York
say means for example, as perhaps does

explanation.surface: A body based in Manhattan might pull out.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsay something is to take back or retract a statement you have made.

clue.text: What lifts non-Christians?

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting a word lets it read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: eh? asks what?
an unclued capital city, as the preamble says: the capital of Greece

explanation.surface: Asking what will raise the spirits of unbelievers.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathens are people who do not hold to a major religion, regarded by Christians as unbelievers.

clue.text: Commander cracks on the subject of something finely poised

indicators.note: to crack something is to break into it, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: re means concerning
OC is the abbreviation for officer commanding
an unclued capital city, as the preamble says: the capital of Jamaica

explanation.surface: An officer breaking under pressure while discussing a delicate balance.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocking stone is a large boulder balanced so delicately that a push makes it rock.

clue.text: Gold stars …

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
an unclued capital city, as the preamble says: the capital of Latvia

explanation.walkthrough: 'Gold stars' looks like a reward chart; the ellipsis carries on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Auriga, the Charioteer, is a northern constellation, a named group of stars.

clue.text: Perhaps SPECTRE agent is an oddball, wearing dodgy syrups

indicators.note: an oddball is out of the ordinary, so these words come out in an odd order
something dodgy is unreliable and not straight, so these letters are scrambled
one piece wears the other, which therefore sits inside it like clothing

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Bond villain's eccentric henchman sporting a cheap wig.
explanation.walkthrough: Syrup is rhyming slang for a wig (syrup of figs), which shapes the surface. SPECTRE is the villains' organisation in the James Bond stories.
explanation.definitionFit: A Soviet agent is one example of a SPECTRE operative, as with Rosa Klebb in From Russia with Love.

clue.text: … for separating an area, of course

indicators.note: a thing that separates two letters stands between them

blocks.note: taken as written
pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: Something that keeps one area apart from another, as you might expect.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the previous clue, but each clue stands alone. 'Of course' is not the throwaway phrase it seems; it means on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf course the apron is the closely mown fringe around the green.

clue.text: Business centre revolutionised by ticking boxes

indicators.note: to box is to enclose, so the words that follow hold the letters
a revolution turns things round, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A financial district transformed by form-filling bureaucrats.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, the Square Mile.
explanation.definitionFit: The City, or a city's financial quarter, is where banks and businesses are concentrated.

clue.text: Prison sentence's upper limit

blocks.note: doing time is serving a prison sentence
an unclued capital city, as the preamble says: the capital of Germany

explanation.surface: A judge's sentence that reaches the maximum allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: The timberline is the altitude above which trees cannot grow on a mountain, the highest boundary of forest.

clue.text: See 9
The taxman's covering letter

indicators.note: the outer words cover and conceal what lies inside them

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A tax inspector sending a cover letter with the demand.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is the seventh character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Leak: phosphorus beginning to appear

blocks.note: to take a leak is slang for to pee
P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus

explanation.surface: A chemistry lab where a phosphorus spill starts to show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leak' looks like an escape of liquid; it is slang for urinating.
explanation.definitionFit: To peep is to start to emerge, showing just a little, as the sun peeps out from cloud.

clue.text: Attempt to evacuate corrupt politicians

indicators.note: evacuating empties out the inside, leaving just the outer shell

blocks.note: a try is an attempt
an unclued capital city, as the preamble says: the capital of Jordan

explanation.surface: Trying to clear out a gang of crooked politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: Tammany Hall was the Democratic machine that ran New York City through patronage and graft.
explanation.definitionFit: Tammany has become a byword for corrupt political organisation, after the New York machine.

clue.text: Order something that's silvery-white on the table

blocks.clueFragment: something that's silvery-white on the table
blocks.note: caesium, symbol Cs, is a silvery-white metal in the periodic table
an unclued capital city, as the preamble says: the capital of Samoa

explanation.surface: Asking for the silver to be laid on the dining table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The table' looks like dinner but is the periodic table.
explanation.definitionFit: A capias is a legal writ ordering an officer to arrest a named person.
